name: Answer calls, book appointments and take messages with a Vapi voice agent and Google Calendar

parameters.content:
## Answer calls, book appointments and take messages with a Vapi voice agent and Google Calendar

### How it works

This workflow is the complete backend for a Vapi voice receptionist at any appointment-based business. One webhook receives every Vapi tool call, a parser normalises the payload, and a switch routes by tool name. `checkAvailability` fetches the coming week's events from Google Calendar and computes real open slots in code — business hours, working days, slot length, minimum notice and a one-slot-per-day spread are all configurable — then hands the agent numbered options with exact ISO ids to book against. `bookAppointment` creates the calendar event, logs it to a call-log sheet and emails the owner. `takeMessage` captures a callback request from callers who don't want to book, logs it and emails the owner. Status updates and end-of-call reports are acknowledged harmlessly. Every tool returns a spoken-ready result to Vapi.

### Setup steps

- In your Vapi assistant, add three server tools pointing at this workflow's production webhook URL: `checkAvailability` (no arguments), `bookAppointment` (arguments: `customerName`, `phoneNumber`, `service`, `startTime` — the ISO id from the offered slots), and `takeMessage` (arguments: `callerName`, `phoneNumber`, `message`).
- Connect a Google Calendar credential on both calendar nodes; the primary calendar is used by default.
- Edit the CONFIGURE block in *Compute Open Slots*: timezone, opening hours, working days, slot length, notice period.
- Connect an SMTP credential on both email nodes and set the From and To addresses.
- Create a Google Sheet with headers `Timestamp`, `Type`, `Caller Name`, `Phone`, `Details`, `When` and select it in both Sheets nodes.
- Activate the workflow and test by calling your Vapi number.

### Customization

Adjust the slot rules, appointment length, email wording and log columns to fit the business — the same three-tool pattern suits salons, clinics, trades, tutors and any business that books time.

## Receive and route

One webhook takes every Vapi tool call. The parser normalises the payload, then the switch routes by tool name — with a safe fallback so status updates never trigger a booking.

## checkAvailability

Fetches the coming week from Google Calendar and computes open slots in code — no LLM needed. Returns numbered options with exact ISO ids for the agent to book against.

## bookAppointment

Creates the event, logs it to the call-log sheet, emails the owner, and confirms back to the caller in plain language.

## takeMessage

Callers who don't want to book leave a message instead — logged to the same sheet and emailed to the owner, so no call ever goes nowhere.

## Everything else

Vapi status updates, transcripts and end-of-call reports are acknowledged and ignored.

nodes.name: Parse Vapi Tool Call
nodes.notes: Normalises every Vapi payload shape into { toolName, toolCallId, args } so routing is one clean comparison.

nodes.name: Compute Open Slots
nodes.notes: All business rules live in the CONFIGURE block: timezone, hours, working days, slot length, notice period and how many slots to offer.

nodes.name: Create Event in Google Calendar
nodes.notes: Appointment length is 30 minutes here — keep it in sync with SLOT_MINS in Compute Open Slots if you change it.

nodes.name: Email Booking Alert to Owner
nodes.notes: Set your From and To addresses. Continues on error so a mail hiccup never breaks the caller's confirmation.
